stories.headline: MARKETS REBOUND 1%+ AHEAD OF FOMC AND Q1 GDP — VISA SURGES 6% ON BLOWOUT EARNINGS
stories.body: S&P 500 rose 1.05% and Nasdaq climbed 1.64%, snapping Tuesday's tech selloff. Visa jumped 6% after reporting 17% revenue growth — its strongest quarter since 2022. Starbucks added 5% on an earnings beat. The FOMC begins its two-day meeting today; no rate change expected from the current 3.5–3.75% target range.

stories.headline: Q1 GDP ADVANCE ESTIMATE DUE TOMORROW — TARIFF IMPORT SURGE MAY PRODUCE MISLEADING CONTRACTION
stories.body: The BEA releases the Q1 2026 GDP advance estimate at 8:30 AM ET Thursday alongside the FOMC decision at 2 PM ET. Imports reportedly surged at a ~38% annualized rate in Q1 as companies front-ran April tariff hikes, which mechanically drags net exports and could produce a negative headline print even if domestic demand held firm.

stories.headline: VISA BEATS ON REVENUE AND EARNINGS — SPENDING DURABILITY INTACT DESPITE TARIFF ENVIRONMENT
stories.body: Visa's 17% revenue growth — the fastest since 2022 — signals that consumer spending has held up despite tariff-driven price pressures and slowing GDP forecasts. The print is a key early read on discretionary demand with four Magnificent Seven companies still set to report this week.

stories.headline: OIL GIVES BACK SOME OF TUESDAY'S 5.8% SPIKE — WTI SETTLES AT $99.32 AS IRAN TENSIONS SIMMER
stories.body: WTI crude fell 1.7% to $99.32 after surging 5.8% on Monday on Iranian supply concerns. Gold dipped to $4,569 (-0.2%) as investors rotated into equities on the risk-on session. The dollar weakened slightly with DXY at 98.4, extending its retreat below the psychologically important 100 level.

stories.headline: MICHIGAN WINS 2026 NCAA CHAMPIONSHIP — FIRST TITLE SINCE 1989, BEATS UCONN 69-63
stories.body: The Wolverines captured their first national championship in 37 years, defeating UConn 69-63 in the title game. Michigan knocked off No. 1 seed Arizona in the Final Four to reach the championship and then held off a late Husky rally to seal the program's second title in the modern era.

stories.headline: FIVE PLAYOFF SERIES IN ACTION TONIGHT — PISTONS, RAPTORS, ROCKETS ALL FACING ELIMINATION OR MUST-WIN SPOTS
stories.body: Wednesday's slate features five high-stakes games: Pistons host Magic in a do-or-die Game 5 (ORL leads 3-1, 7 PM ET); Cavaliers host Raptors in a tied Game 5 (7:30 PM ET); Knicks hold 3-2 series lead vs. Hawks; Lakers lead Rockets 3-1; Thunder (already advanced) cleared the way for a wide-open West bracket.

stories.headline: 2026 NFL DRAFT COMPLETE — RAIDERS SELECT INDIANA QB FERNANDO MENDOZA #1 OVERALL
stories.body: Las Vegas took Fernando Mendoza with the top pick in Pittsburgh, making him the first Hoosier QB ever drafted first overall. Nine offensive linemen went in Round 1 — the most in a single round in recent memory. The Seahawks selected Notre Dame RB Jadarian Price at #32; the Cardinals added Carson Beck in Round 3.

stories.headline: SPRING CAMPS WRAPPING ACROSS POWER FOUR — CLEMSON DROPS FIVE IN WAY-TOO-EARLY TOP 25
stories.body: Power Four programs are completing spring practices. ESPN's updated way-too-early rankings show Clemson falling five spots to No. 24 following a disappointing spring. Defending national champion Indiana is positioned as a top-10 team and visits Washington on Nov. 21 — the third straight year the Huskies host the defending champs.

deepDive.title: How Tariff Front-Running Distorts GDP — Why Tomorrow's Number May Mislead
content: Tomorrow's Q1 2026 GDP advance estimate arrives with an important asterisk. The quarter coincides precisely with the window when U.S. companies raced to import goods before April's tariff hikes took effect — and preliminary data suggest imports surged at roughly a 38% annualized rate. If confirmed in the official BEA release, the headline GDP figure could print negative or near-zero — not because the domestic economy collapsed, but because of how the national accounts are arithmetically constructed. Markets rallied today partly on the premise that savvy investors will look past the distorted headline.

The mechanism is purely mechanical. GDP is defined as C + I + G + NX, where NX (net exports) equals exports minus imports. When imports spike for any reason, NX becomes more negative, directly subtracting from the total. A firm that imported $500 million in steel ahead of a tariff deadline registers as a $500 million drag on that quarter's GDP — even though that steel will enter domestic production and appear as positive investment activity in Q2. The national accounts record flows as they occur with no adjustment for the underlying motive. This is why economists consistently flag 'real final sales to domestic purchasers' — a metric that strips out the volatile net exports component entirely — as a cleaner proxy for underlying demand when trade distortions are large. Watch that sub-component specifically in tomorrow's release.

Historical precedent supports skepticism about the headline. In Q1 2022, GDP printed -1.5% annualized, triggering recession warnings across Wall Street. Yet the economy added 1.7 million jobs that same quarter — the labor market and the GDP headline were telling completely different stories, largely because a post-pandemic import surge was mechanically crushing net exports. The pattern repeated in Q1 2025, when the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow briefly tracked below zero on similar front-running dynamics before Q2 data fully reversed the trade drag. Goldman Sachs estimated the Q1 2026 trade distortion alone could subtract 3–4 percentage points from the annualized growth rate, implying an 'underlying' economy growing closer to 2% may still print as a contraction.

For markets, interpretation will hinge on the internal breakdown. If gross private domestic investment and consumer spending components look solid, a bad headline print may actually trigger a rally — it signals mean-reversion ahead as imports normalize and net exports swing back positive in Q2. The Fed, announcing at 2 PM ET the same day, will almost certainly signal it sees through the distortion and reaffirm its data-dependent hold. The strategic setup heading into Q2 is arguably bullish: firms that pre-loaded inventories are better positioned against the tariff shock, import volumes will mechanically normalize, and any Q2 GDP print is likely to look significantly stronger — setting up a narrative of recovery even as underlying conditions may not have changed materially.
